question.problem:
Consider the vector space ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$ of all $2\times 2$ matrices over $R.$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a linearly independent set in ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$

II. $[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$ can be expressed as a linear combination of $\{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $\{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is false. Notice that

$$
0\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

where some coefficients are nonzero, so the set is linearly dependent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]=(-1)\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+0\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- Statement III is false. Since the set is not linearly independent, it can't form a basis.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
